chunks: Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Sama'ah from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed the Hajj Tawaf and the Women's Tawaf before running between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. He said: 'It does not harm him; he runs between As-Safa and Al-Marwah after he has completed his Hajj.'
And Ishaq said, and Sama'ah narrated a similar thing from Sulayman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

key_terms.لَا يَضُرُّهُ: It does not harm him (is valid)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs Tawaf before Sa'i?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that performing Tawaf al-Hajj and Tawaf al-Nisa before Sa'i does not invalidate the Hajj, reflecting the Shia view of flexibility in the order of rituals (Tartibi vs. Irtibati). This ruling emphasizes that the essential pillars are preserved even if the recommended sequence is altered, allowing the pilgrim to simply complete the Sa'i afterwards. This highlights the practical leniency in Shia fiqh regarding ritual order, distinguishing it from stricter interpretations that might require repetition.
